A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SD-truthfulness, rounding, and enforced-agreement study. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching extensively relocated material.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original sensitivity and budgetary-efficiency simulations using information structures estimated from crowdsourcing datasets.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix E retain original sensitivity evaluations and report budgetary-efficiency simulations with threshold payments.

M1.justification: Direct rounding, partition rounding, and EA's enforced distributions, report flipping, and agreement scoring are retained. The general-signal integer-programming enforcement and optimal-enforcement rule move to Appendix C. Changed payment schemes concern the effort-elicitation evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions use binary compound-synthesis judgments and four-class tweet sentiment, with the same crowdsourcing-derived information structures. Prior sweeps, task-count sweeps, and multi-agent effort elicitation remain; reward functions and target effort values change within this coverage.

E2.justification: OA, PTS, CA, MA, and their existing partitioned or rounded variants remain in the comparisons. Original implementations move into Appendix E.2. The budgetary-efficiency plots retain the same six mechanism variants and optimal-linear-payment reference.

E3.justification: Section 7.3 replaces winner-take-all and Borda-count tournaments with fixed-threshold bonuses. Target efforts change from 0.7 and 0.9 to 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, and 0.9. V2 splits 10,000 simulations equally between estimating a 75th-percentile threshold and evaluating payments, substantially revising the payment-evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The practical robustness check linking sensitivity to budgetary efficiency is substantially revised: tournament-based validation is replaced by threshold-payment validation across four effort levels. Enforcement-choice, prior-sensitivity, and task-count analyses remain. Appendix E.2 reorganizes the existing original-versus-rounded comparison rather than introducing a new ablation.

E5.justification: Section 7.1 newly specifies 20,000 independent Monte Carlo score samples, where v1 specified only T repetitions. This discloses a count without establishing an increase in runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-based variability.

E6.justification: V1 Figure 3's tournament-payment outcomes are replaced by v2 Figure 2's threshold-payment outcomes at four effort levels. EA-prior remains the lowest-payment mechanism among those plotted. These are substantially replaced results under different reward conditions, not evidence of a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: New Appendix A supplies explicit failure arguments for f-mutual-information, determinant-mutual-information, and pairing mechanisms, extending v1's largely intuitive discussion. The central rounding, binary and three-signal EA, optimal-enforcement, and MA results and proofs are retained after relocation.

C1.justification: The central SD-truthfulness, partition-rounding, and binary-EA contributions remain. Practical applicability is narrowed: tournaments used as a motivating application in v1 are replaced by threshold rewards, and v2's conclusion explicitly leaves tournament incentive guarantees unresolved.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly explains that correlated scores can let a dominated reporting strategy improve tournament rank, correcting v1's interpretation that SD-truthfulness supports tournament payments. It also adds a variance-control explanation for EA. Conversely, it removes v1's warning that optimal enforcement may overfit the simplified effort model.

D1.justification: V2 adds an experimental-code repository link, specifies the sensitivity simulation count, and documents threshold calibration and evaluation. However, v1 Appendix C.1's prior-sweep joint-distribution matrix and 0.01 step size disappear. The dataset information-structure parameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds focused comparisons with mutual-information mechanisms that v1 placed beyond detailed discussion. The Lu et al. (2024) citation is removed. The main research positioning and attribution of binary rounding to Miller et al. (2005) remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction, model exposition, and mechanism discussion are rewritten and condensed. Sensitivity derivations, non-binary EA, optimal enforcement, and proofs are reorganized into Appendices A–F. Broader Impact and Acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a conference template with substantially different typography and title layout. Sensitivity plots are merged into a three-panel main figure and separated into four appendix panels; tournament plots are replaced by threshold-payment panels. Table 1 and plot legends are reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important validity problem in v1's practical argument: SD-truthfulness was treated as sufficient for tournament incentives. Section 8 explains the correlated-score limitation, and Section 7.3 replaces tournaments with fixed-threshold rewards calibrated and evaluated on separate samples. This substantially improves alignment between the theoretical guarantee and experimental application, outweighing the loss of prior-sweep documentation and the optimal-enforcement caveat.
